rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision from the heavens is rain, and that from the earth is vegetation.
rows.anchor: المطر { و } من { الأرض } النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone provides those things; this question and answer is an argument against the idolaters.
rows.anchor: أي: الذي يفعل ذلك الله، وهذا احتجاج عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indirectly challenges them: one side is lying, while the intended charge is that they are astray for associating partners with their Provider.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما تقول لصاحبك إذا كذب: أحدنا كاذب، وتعنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of separation from their deeds resembles the statement, “You have your religion, and I have mine.”
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله تعالى: لكم دينكم ولي دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather the two sides on the Resurrection and judge between them justly; He is the Opener, the Knowing.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر أنه يجمعهم في القيامة، ثم يحكم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sea is intensely sweet, while the other is intensely bitter; fish is eaten from both, and coral is extracted from the salt sea as jewelry.
rows.anchor: هذا عذب فرات } شديد العذوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of fresh fish and wearable coral from the seas demonstrates God's power.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر هذا للدلالة على قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitmir is the thin covering around a date stone.
rows.anchor: من قطمير } يعني: لفافة النواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection Day, the beings worshipped as partners will disown the worshippers, saying that they were not worshipped by them.
rows.anchor: أي: يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expert who gives this true report is God, exalted is He.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبئك مثل خبير } وهو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people took the messengers as an ill omen because rain had been withheld, and threatened to stone them to death if they did not stop.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم حبس عنهم المطر، فقالوا: هذا بشؤمكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their threat to stone the messengers means they would kill them by pelting them with stones.
rows.anchor: لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم } لنقتلنكم رجما بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people's ill fortune was their own disbelief; when admonished, they treated the warning as an omen, though they were transgressing through idolatry.
rows.anchor: طائركم معكم } شؤمكم معكم بكفركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from the far end of the city was Habib al-Najjar, a believer in the messengers who lived at the city's edge.
rows.anchor: وهو حبيب النجار، كان قد آمن بالرسل، وكان منزله في أقصى البلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Habib heard that the people had denied the messengers and meant to kill them, he came to urge the people to believe.
rows.anchor: فلما سمع أن القوم كذبوهم وهموا بقتلهم أتاهم يأمرهم بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers seek no payment for giving counsel and delivering the message; “they are guided” refers to the messengers.
rows.anchor: على أداء النصح وتبليغ الرسالة { وهم مهتدون } يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habib responds that he should worship the One who created him, to whom they will all return.
rows.anchor: مالي لا أعبد الذي فطرني وإليه ترجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters hope their gods will protect them from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: يمنعون من عذاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot help their worshippers; both worshippers and idols are brought into the Fire, with the idols accompanying them there.
rows.anchor: آلهتهم { وهم لهم جند محضرون }. في النار؛ لأن أوثانهم معهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ugly words about Muhammad should not grieve him: God knows what they conceal and reveal and will requite them for it.
rows.anchor: فيك بالسوء والقبيح. { إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون } فنجازيهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being in this verse is al-As ibn Wa'il.
rows.anchor: أنا خلقناه من نطفة } يعني: العاص بن وائل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification of the human being is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وائل. وقيل: أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He became an outspoken disputant arguing falsely with the Prophet against resurrection.
rows.anchor: جدل بالباطل، خاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إنكار البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier asks how God can revive great, crumbled bones but forgets his own first creation; remembering it would have kept him from denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: ونسي ابتداء خلقه؛ لأنه لو علم ذلك ما أنكر الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who created the bones initially can revive them, and He knows every creation, both its beginning and its return.
rows.anchor: خلقها { أول مرة وهو بكل خلق } من الابتداء والإعادة { عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green trees are al-marakh and al-afar, from which Arabs made fire sticks and kindled fire.
rows.anchor: يعني: المرخ والعفار، ومنهما زنود الأعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator of the heavens and earth is certainly able to create beings like them again.
rows.anchor: ثم احتج عليهم بخلق السموات والأرض، فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God wills to create something, He commands it to be, and that thing comes to be.
rows.anchor: أي: خلق شيء { أن يقول له كن فيكون } ذلك الشيء

words: فَسُبْحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِى بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above any description that denies His ability to resurrect; His hand holds power over everything, and all return to Him in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: تنزيها لله سبحانه من أن يوصف بغير القدرة على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected letter Sad is glossed as “God has spoken truth.”
rows.anchor: ص } صدق الله { والقرآن ذي الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran possesses honor and renown.
rows.anchor: والقرآن ذي الذكر } ذي الشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “might” is refusal to accept religion; their “schism” is opposition and enmity.
rows.anchor: في عزة } امتناع من الدين { وشقاق } خلاف وعداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How many We destroyed” is the answer to the oath, with the intervening statement about disbelievers interrupting the two parts.
rows.anchor: هذا جواب القسم، اعترض بينهما قوله: { بل الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the moment of destruction, they cried out seeking rescue; it was no time to escape or find refuge.
rows.anchor: بالاستغاثة عند الهلاك { ولات حين مناص } وليس حين منجى وفوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who marveled were the people of Mecca, and their warner from among them was Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني: أهل مكة { أن جاءهم منذر منهم } محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans gathered at Abu Talib's home to complain about the Prophet; when he called them to the confession of God's oneness, they asked how one god could suffice all creation.
rows.anchor: اجتمعوا عند أبي طالب يشكون إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called the Prophet's claim astonishing and strange.
rows.anchor: الذي يقوله { لشيء عجاب } عجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs rose from that gathering and urged one another to continue worshipping their gods; they saw Muhammad's call as a plot aimed at them.
rows.anchor: نهضوا من مجلسهم ذلك، يقول بعضهم لبعض: { امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” means the Prophet's teaching, which they say they had not heard in the inherited religion of their forefathers.
rows.anchor: ما سمعنا بهذا } الذي يقوله { في الملة الآخرة } فيما أدركنا عليه آباءنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilaq means a fabrication, falsehood, and lie.
rows.anchor: إن هذا إلا اختلاق } زور وكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection asks why Muhammad alone was chosen for revelation; the author attributes it to envy of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: كيف خص بالوحي من جملتنا؟ قالوا هذا حسدا له على النبوة

words: بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God identifies their real state as doubt about His revelation, despite their calling it fabrication; tasting punishment would make them certain.
rows.anchor: أي: وحيي [أي:حين قالوا: اختلاق] { بل لما يذوقوا عذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether they possess the keys to prophethood and can grant it to whomever they choose.
rows.anchor: أي: مفاتيح النبوة حتى يعطوا النبوة من اختاروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God channels rainwater into springs in the earth; all water in the earth has descended from heaven.
rows.anchor: وهي المواضع التي ينبع منها الماء، وكل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water brings forth crops of different colors; they dry, turn yellow, and crumble into fragments, signs for the reflective of God's oneness and power.
rows.anchor: يذكرون ما لهم من الدلالة في هذا على توحيد الله تعالى وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's expanding a person's chest means making it spacious for Islam and guiding that person to the religion.
rows.anchor: وسعه { للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه } أي: فاهتدى إلى دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following warning about hardened hearts supplies the unstated comparison: the guided person is unlike one whose heart is sealed.
rows.anchor: كمن طبع على قلبه، ويدل على هذا المحذوف قوله: { فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's passages resemble one another without contradiction; it repeats accounts and stories, and mentions reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا من غير اختلاف ولا تناقض { مثاني } يثني فيه الأخبار والقصص

words: تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skin shivers in fear when a punishment verse is recited, then skin and heart soften toward God at a verse of mercy; fear and hope constitute God's guidance.
rows.anchor: يعني: عند ذكر آية العذاب { ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله } أي: من آية الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever is thrown into the Fire bound and can ward it off only with his face; the rhetorical comparison is with someone who enters Paradise.
rows.anchor: وهو الكافر يلقي في النار مغلولا، فلا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant God suffices is Muhammad; God supports him and protects him from his enemies.
rows.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلوات الله عليه، ينصره ويكفيه أمر من يعاديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters threatened Muhammad with their idols, saying that because he insulted them they would harm him; despite worshipping idols, they admitted God is the Creator.
rows.anchor: يخوفونك بأوثانهم، يقولون: إنك لتعيبها، وإنها لتصيبنك بسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boastful recipient says he was given wealth because of his own distinction and merit, believing he knew he would receive it through deserving it.
rows.anchor: أعطيته على شرف وفضل، وكنت علمت أني سأعطى هذا باستحقاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift is a test from God to see whether the servant gives thanks or disbelieves.
rows.anchor: أي: تلك العطية فتنة من الله تعالى يبتلي به العبد ليشكر أو يكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier person who made this boast was Qarun, who said he had received his wealth through his own knowledge.
rows.anchor: يعني: قارون حين قال: إنما أوتيته على علم عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups and successive companies.
rows.anchor: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا } جماعات وأفواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses came, Pharaoh ordered the renewed killing of Israelite boys to deter the people from following him.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن فرعون أمر بإعادة القتل على الذكور من أولاد بني إسرائيل لما أتاه موسى

words: وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's scheme and evil conduct come to nothing and perish.
rows.anchor: مكر فرعون وسوء صنيعه { إلا في ضلال } زوال وبطلان وذهاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells his chiefs to let him kill Moses and challenges Moses to call on the Lord who sent him to protect him.
rows.anchor: وقال فرعون } لملئه: { ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه } الذي أرسله إلينا، فيمنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims to fear that Moses will abolish their religion or corrupt it for them if he cannot abolish it.
rows.anchor: الذين أنتم عليه يبطله { أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد } أو يفسد عليكم دينكم إن لم يبطله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks God's protection from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: فلما توعده بالقتل قال موسى: { إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unassigned reported interpretation takes “some of what he promises” to mean all that he promises.
rows.anchor: يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم } قيل: كل الذي يعدكم

words: لَكُمُ ٱلْمُلْكُ ٱلْيَوْمَ ظَٰهِرِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer reminds them that they currently rule Egypt, dominant over the Israelites, and asks who could protect them from God's punishment if it came.
rows.anchor: أعلمهم أن لهم الملك ظاهرين عالين على بني إسرائيل في أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When prevented from killing Moses, Pharaoh claimed to offer the people only the judgment and advice he would choose for himself.
rows.anchor: حين منع من قتله: { ما أريكم } من الرأي والنصيحة { إلا ما أرى } لنفسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in the Fire plead with Hell's keepers to ask God to lessen their punishment for one day.
rows.anchor: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the inmates acknowledge that messengers brought them proofs, the keepers tell them to pray for themselves; the keepers will not pray for them.
rows.anchor: أي: فادعوا أنتم إذا، فإنا لن ندعو الله لكم

words: وَمَا دُعَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation of the disbelievers is futile and fruitless because it does not benefit them.
rows.anchor: هلاك وبطلان؛ لأنه لا ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God helps His messengers and believers in this life by making their proof prevail, and avenges them against opponents in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: بظهور حجتهم، والانتصار ممن عاداهم بالعذاب في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witnesses who stand are the angels who record the deeds of human beings.
rows.anchor: الملائكة الذين يكتبون أعمال بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istawa here means to set out for or attend to the creation of the heaven, which was vapor rising from water.
rows.anchor: قصد وعمد { إلى } خلق { السماء وهي دخان } بخار مرتفع عن الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands heaven and earth to produce their benefits for creation: the heavens' sun, moon, and stars, and the earth's water and fruit; both obey willingly.
rows.anchor: بما خلقت فيكما من المنافع، وأخرجاها لمنافع خلقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God completed and perfected the seven heavens in two days and instructed the inhabitants of each heaven in His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: صنعهن وأحكمهن { سبع سموات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها } أوحى في أهل كل سماء بما أراد من الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are guarded from devils listening, with stars serving as the protection.
rows.anchor: حفظناها من استماع الشياطين بالكواكب حفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away after this clarification, Muhammad is to warn them of a destructive blast like those that struck earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: عن الإيمان بعد هذا البيان { فقل أنذرتكم } خوفتكم { صاعقة } مهلكة تنزل بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers came to those people and to their predecessors, and messengers also came to the same people after those sent to their forefathers.
rows.anchor: أتت الرسل إياهم ومن كان قبلهم { ومن خلفهم } ومن بعد الرسل الذين أرسلوا إلى آبائهم جاءتهم الرسل أنفسهم

words: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people saying that the Quran was invented by the Prophet are the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: بل أيقولون، يعني: أهل مكة { افترى على الله كذبا } تقول القرآن من قبل نفسه

words: فَإِن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, sealing the Prophet's heart means binding it to patience in the face of their abuse.
rows.anchor: يربط على قلبك بالصبر على أذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This begins a new statement: God erases falsehood, meaning idolatry, and establishes truth through the Quran revealed on His Prophet's tongue.
rows.anchor: ثم ابتدأ فقال { ويمح الله الباطل } أي: الشرك { ويحق الحق بكلماته }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts the servant's return from disobedience to obedience and pardons past sins.
rows.anchor: إذا رجع العبد عن معصية الله تعالى إلى طاعته قبل ذلك الرجوع، وعفا عنه ما سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the requests of those who believe.
rows.anchor: { ويستجيب الذين آمنوا } أي: يجيبهم إلى ما يسألون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God made provision abundant for all His servants, they would transgress and disobey; instead, He apportions it, making some poor and others rich, with knowledge and sight of His servants.
rows.anchor: لطغوا وعصوا { ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء } فيجعل واحدا فقيرا، وآخر غنيا

words: يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْغَيْثَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain after people despair of its coming and spreads His mercy by extending the rain.
rows.anchor: المطر { من بعد ما قنطوا } من بعد يأس العباد من نزوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh made his Coptic people out to be ignorant, and they obeyed him; they were a sinful people.
rows.anchor: فاستخف قومه } وجد قومه القبط جهالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Pharaoh's people angered God by disbelieving, He took vengeance on them.
rows.anchor: فلما آسفونا } أغضبونا بكفرهم. { انتقمنا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them precedents in destruction as a warning to those who came after, and an example for later generations.
rows.anchor: متقدمين في الهلاك [ليتعظ] بهم من بعدهم { ومثلا للآخرين } عبرة لمن يجيء بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 21:98 was revealed, disbelievers argued that they accepted their idols being likened to Jesus; Muslims protested until 21:101 was revealed, and this surah retells the story.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية حين خاصمه الكفار لما نزل قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasidun means they make a loud uproar; the Muslims protested at the comparison with their idols.
rows.anchor: أي: يضجون، وذلك أن المسلمين ضجوا من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is the one God has shown mercy: God will give that person help.
rows.anchor: إلا من رحم } لكن من رحم الله فإنه ينصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zaqqum tree is the food of the sinful person, whom al-Wahidi identifies here as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: طعام الأثيم } أي: صاحب الإثم، وهو أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The food is like molten silver or copper in its heat, boiling in its eaters' bellies like scalding water.
rows.anchor: أي: كالذائب من الفضة والنحاس في الحرارة. { يغلي في البطون } في بطون آكليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner is driven along roughly and forcefully to the middle of Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني: الأثيم { فاعتلوه } سوقوه [سوقا] بالعنف { إلى سواء الجحيم } وسط الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pouring of boiling water over his head is also described in 22:19.
rows.anchor: صبوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم } كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt echoes Abu Jahl's own boast that nobody between the two mountains was more powerful or generous than he was.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه قال: ما بين جبليها أعز ولا أكرم مني

words: إِنَّ هَٰذَا مَا كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَمْتَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment before them is what they had doubted.
rows.anchor: إن هذا } الذي ترون من العذاب { ما كنتم به تمترون } فيه تشكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous dwell in a secure place, safe from harm.
rows.anchor: إن المتقين في مقام أمين } أمنوا فيه من الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water of Paradise has no change in its smell, and its wine is pleasant to drink.
rows.anchor: غير آسن } غير متغير الرائحة { وأنهار من خمر لذة للشاربين } لذيذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who listen to the Prophet and then ask what he said are hypocrites.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يستمع إليك } يعني: المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listened to the Prophet's sermon, then mockingly asked his Companions what he had just said, signaling that they had paid no attention.
rows.anchor: كانوا يستمعون خطبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وإذا خرجوا سألوا أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean that God granted them the reward for their piety.
rows.anchor: وآتاهم تقواهم } أي: ثواب تقواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means that God inspired them with piety and enabled them to practice it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: وألهمهم تقواهم ووفقهم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is sinful to suspect evil of good people or of anyone not known to be wicked.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يظن السوء بأهل الخير، وبمن لا يعلم منه فسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not seek out Muslims' private faults or investigate their defects.
rows.anchor: لا تطلبوا عورات المسلمين، ولا تبحثوا عن معايبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Backbiting is mentioning something about someone that they would dislike, even when it is true of them.
rows.anchor: لا تذكروا أحدكم بشيء يكرهه وإن كان فيه ذلك الشيء

words: أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking ill of an absent brother is likened to eating his dead flesh, which he cannot feel; disliking that image should lead one to reject backbiting.
rows.anchor: يعني: إن ذكرك أخاك على غيبة بسوء كأكل لحمه وهو ميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people descend from the same father and mother, so lineage gives no basis for superiority.
rows.anchor: أي: كلكم بنو أب واحد وأم واحدة، فلا تفاضل بينكم في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿub are the heads of tribes, such as Rabi'a and Mudar; tribes are subdivisions, such as Bakr of Rabi'a and Tamim of Mudar.
rows.anchor: وهي رؤوس القبائل، كربيعة ومضر { وقبائل } وهي دون الشعوب كبكر من ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peoples and tribes exist so people can recognize degrees of kinship, near and distant, not to boast about ancestry.
rows.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب وبعده لا لتتفاخروا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most honored person before God is the one most mindful of Him.
rows.anchor: ثم أعلم أن أرفعهم عنده منزلة أتقاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tubba was a king in Yemen who accepted Islam and called his people to it, but they rejected him; God's threat of punishment therefore came true against them.
rows.anchor: وهو ملك كان باليمن أسلم، ودعا قومه إلى الإسلام فكذبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God was not incapable of the first creation and so will not become incapable of recreating people; their doubt concerns resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي: أعجزنا عنه حتى نعيى بالإعادة { بل هم في لبس } شك { من خلق جديد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul's whisper is what the person's heart tells him.
rows.anchor: ولقد خلقنا الإنسان ونعلم ما توسوس به نفسه } يحدثه قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to the person than the jugular vein by His knowledge; the vein is in the neck.
rows.anchor: بالعلم { من حبل الوريد } وهو عرق في العنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two receiving angels are guardians who take note of a person's deeds and record them.
rows.anchor: أي: الملكان الحافظان يتلقيان ويأخذان ما يعمله الإنسان، فيثبتانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One angel sits on each side of the person.
rows.anchor: عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد } قاعدان على جانبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every spoken word has an angel present to watch and preserve it.
rows.anchor: ما يلفظ } يتكلم { من قول إلا لديه رقيب } حافظ { عتيد } حاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stupor is death's overpowering intensity; “with the truth” means the person sees the realities of the Hereafter plainly, and this is the death he evaded.
rows.anchor: أي:غمرته وشدته { بالحق } أي: من أمر الآخرة حتى يراه الإنسان عيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil companion says he did not mislead the person: the person was already far astray and chose to answer the devil's invitation.
rows.anchor: من الشياطين: { ربنا ما أطغيته } ما أضللته { ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids them to argue before Him and says He had warned them of punishment through the messengers.
rows.anchor: حذرتكم العقوبة في الدنيا على لسان الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's decree is not changed, and He does not break His promise or punish servants without wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: لا تبديل لقولي ولا خلف لوعدي { وما أنا بظلام للعبيد } فأعاقب بغير جرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question to Hell confirms that it has been filled as promised; Hell's question about more space means there is none left.
rows.anchor: وهذا استفهام تحقيق، وذلك أن الله عز وجل وعدها أن يملأها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is brought near for the mindful, so they can see it; it is not far from them.
rows.anchor: أدنيت الجنة { للمتقين } حتى يروها { غير بعيد } منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their “engagement” is falsehood, and their play is being distracted by their disbelief.
rows.anchor: في خوض } باطل { يلعبون } أي: تشاغلهم بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are shoved toward Hell with a forceful, violent push.
rows.anchor: يدفعون إليها دفعا عنيفا

words: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told that the Fire in front of them is the very punishment they had denied.
rows.anchor: ويقال لهم: { هذه النار التي كنتم بها تكذبون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke: now that they see it, do they really believe in God's punishment?
rows.anchor: وهذا توبيخ لهم، والمعنى: أتصدقون الآن عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star that sets is the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: والنجم إذا هوى } أي: والثريا إذا سقطت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view identifies the star as the Quran, descending in separate portions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القرآن إذا نزل متفرقا نجوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet who did not stray is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ما ضل صاحبكم } محمد عليه السلام { وما غوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the Prophet says is not speech arising from his own whim.
rows.anchor: ما الذي يتكلم به مما قاله بهواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's message is revelation sent to him.
rows.anchor: ما هو { إلا وحي يوحى } إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who taught Muhammad is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: علمه شديد القوى } أي: جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu mirrah means possessed of great strength; Gabriel then assumed the form in which God created him.
rows.anchor: قوة شديدة { فاستوى } جبريل عليه السلام في صورته التي خلقه الله عز وجل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asked to see Gabriel in his original form and arranged a meeting at Hira; Gabriel appeared from the east and filled the horizon from east to west.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سأله أن يريه نفسه على صورته، فواعده ذلك بحراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase reverses the order of events: Gabriel first descended from the sky and then drew near Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هذا من المقلوب، أي: ثم تدلى أي: نزل من السماء، فدنا من محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Muhammad was awed by Gabriel's immense form, God returned Gabriel to human form and brought him close to Muhammad for the revelation.
rows.anchor: بعد ما رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من عظمه، وهاله ذلك رده الله تعالى إلى صورة آدمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is Muhammad; what was revealed is what God revealed to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { ما أوحى } الله عز وجل إلى جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Night Journey, God placed Muhammad's sight in his heart so that he saw God; the vision was real, not an illusion.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله جعل بصره لفي فؤاده حتى رآه، وحقق الله تعالى تلك الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes those who dispute whether Muhammad saw God.
rows.anchor: أفتجادلونه في أنه رأى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies the one seen as Muhammad's Lord.
rows.anchor: ولقد رآه } ربه. وقيل: رأى جبريل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative view says Muhammad saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رأى جبريل على صورته التي خلق عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lote Tree is where created beings' knowledge ends; what lies beyond is unseen and known only to God.
rows.anchor: وهي شجرة إليها ينتهي علم الخلق، وما وراءها غيب لا يعلمه إلا الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jannat al-Ma'wa is the garden to which the souls of martyrs go.
rows.anchor: وهي جنة تصير إليها أرواح الشهداء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view says golden moths cover the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: قيل: يغشاها فراش من ذهب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view says angels resembling crows cover the Lote Tree.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الملائكة أمثال الغربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes Muhammad's proper conduct during the Night Journey: his gaze did not turn from its appointed object or exceed what he was permitted.
rows.anchor: هذا وصف أدب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة المعراج، أي: لم يمل بصره عما قصد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the Hereafter and this world belong to God, and nothing occurs in either except by His will.
rows.anchor: فلا يجري في الدارين إلا ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even angels, more honored by God than idols, cannot intercede for anyone unless God permits it for someone He wills and approves.
rows.anchor: هو أكرم على الله من هذه الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject the Hereafter call the angels daughters of God.
rows.anchor: تسمية الأنثى } يقولون: إنهم بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no knowledge of their claim, follow only conjecture, and their conjecture cannot avert punishment.
rows.anchor: إن ظنهم لا يدفع عنهم من العذاب شيئا

words: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to turn away from the person who turns away from the Quran and seeks only the worldly life.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن القرآن { ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their knowledge reaches only this point: they have preferred this world to the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يقول: ذلك نهاية علمهم أن آثروا الدنيا على الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-lamam means minor sins, such as a glance or a kiss.
rows.anchor: يعني: صغار الذنوب، كالنظرة والقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creating people from earth refers to creating their forefather from dust; ajinnah is the plural of janin, an embryo.
rows.anchor: يعني: خلق أباكم من التراب { وإذ أنتم أجنة } جمع جنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not praise yourselves; God knows best who is mindful and does good.
rows.anchor: لا تمدحوها { هو أعلم بمن اتقى } عمل حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who turned away from belief was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: أعرض عن الإيمان، يعني: الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Walid accepted the Prophet's message, a polytheist rebuked him; al-Walid feared punishment, then returned to shirk when promised that another would bear his punishment for payment.
rows.anchor: وكان قد اتبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فعيره بعض المشركين على ذلك فقال: إني أخشى عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walid gave the guarantor only part of what he had promised, then stopped and withheld the remainder.
rows.anchor: فرجع في الشرك وأعطى صاحبه الضامن من بعض ما كان ضمن له، ومنعه الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether he has unseen knowledge of the Hereafter that lets him know someone else will carry his punishment.
rows.anchor: ما غاب عنه من أمر الآخرة، حتى علم أن غيره يحمل عنه العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scriptures of Moses are the books of the Torah.
rows.anchor: أم لم ينبأ بما في صحف موسى } أسفار التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham fulfilled completely everything he had been commanded to do.
rows.anchor: أكمل ما أمر به وأتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul is held accountable for another soul's sin.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تؤخذ نفس بمأثم غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person has only the work he has done for his Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى } عمل لآخرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's work, both good and evil, will be seen in his balance.
rows.anchor: وأن سعيه } عمله { سوف يرى } في ميزانه من خير وشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will then be repaid with the fullest recompense.
rows.anchor: ثم يجزاه } يجزى عليه { الجزاء الأوفى } الأتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final destination and return are to God.
rows.anchor: وأن إلى ربك المنتهى } المصير والمرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes whichever of His creatures He wills laugh and whichever He wills weep.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو أضحك } من شاء من خلقه { وأبكى } من شاء منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death in this world and gives life for the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو أمات } في الدنيا { وأحيا } للبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to semen being poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: إذا تمنى } أي: تصب في الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second creation is the new creation after death.
rows.anchor: وأن عليه النشأة الأخرى } الخلق الآخر بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriches people with money; one explanation of aqna is that He makes them content with what He has given.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو أغنى } بالمال { وأقنى } أرضى بما أعطى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative meaning of aqna is that God gives principal assets and property kept as lasting wealth.
rows.anchor: أرضى بما أعطى. وقيل: أقنى: أعطى أصول الأموال وما يتخذ فيه قنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shi'ra is a star behind al-Jawza that was worshipped in the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: وهي كوكب خلف الجوازاء كانت تعبد في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first people of Ad were the people of Hud.
rows.anchor: وأنه أهلك عادا الأولى } قوم هود
